# quay_organization_robot_federation (Resource)

Manages the OIDC federation configuration for an organization robot account. This allows a robot to be authenticated using tokens issued by an external OIDC provider (keyless / SSO robot federation). The set of federation rules is managed as a whole; applying this resource replaces the robot's entire federation configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "quay_organization" "main" {
  name  = "main"
  email = "quay+main@example.com"
}

resource "quay_organization_robot" "ci" {
  name    = "ci"
  orgname = quay_organization.main.name
}

# Allow the robot to be authenticated (keyless) via OIDC tokens from an
# external identity provider instead of using its static token.
resource "quay_organization_robot_federation" "ci" {
  orgname   = quay_organization.main.name
  robotname = quay_organization_robot.ci.name

  federation = [
    {
      issuer  = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
      subject = "repo:my-org/my-repo:ref:refs/heads/main"
    },
    {
      issuer  = "https://accounts.google.com"
      subject = "1234567890"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `federation` (Attributes List) The list of OIDC federation rules for the robot. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--federation))
- `orgname` (String) The name of the organization that owns the robot.
- `robotname` (String) The short name of the robot (without the organization prefix).

<a id="nestedatt--federation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `federation`

Required:

- `issuer` (String) The issuer (`iss` claim) of the OIDC token, e.g. `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`.
- `subject` (String) The subject (`sub` claim) of the OIDC token that is permitted to authenticate as this robot.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Robot federation configuration can be imported using "<orgname>/<robotname>".
terraform import quay_organization_robot_federation.ci main/ci
```
